chapter_theme: Songs at Thenserigiri (தென்சேரிகிரி): the poet asks to be freed from courtesans who give their lips and take a man's wealth and life, and from the infatuation of dancing women, and asks for the meaning once told to Siva; the praise dwells on Krishna's flute, the gopis' clothes and Kamsa.

614.reading: The poet gives the women's own words, offered to whoever comes, 'here, the one who cannot bear your passion', 'here, take my sweet lips', with eyes dancing and desire melting, and says they take every possession and life without hesitation; he asks for the cool grace that frees him from the sea they call the good of music and lovemaking. The praise names Krishna who took conch and discus, followed the cattle playing the bamboo flute and climbed the tree with the clothes of the women, Brahma bewildered, the gods freed from prison and the demons beaten, at Thenserigiri.
614.nuance: As in 21, the courtesans' speech is quoted (இங்கே வருக, இந்தா), and the charge is that they strip a man of wealth and life alike (பொருள் உயிர்கள் ... பறிகொளும்). சங்கீத கலவி நலம் என்று ஓதும் உததி: the ocean they call the delight of song and love.

615.reading: The poet lists women's cajoling speech, eyes, hair heavy with flowers, breasts like Meru, the posture of their display and slender waists, as they dance with many, like peacocks, and asks Murugan, to free him from the delusion of desire for them, to grant the meaning he told Siva of old, from the ancient Veda, ending all arguments. The praise names the lord of Vayalur's fields, nephew of the cloud-dark one who kicked Kamsa, the six-faced god holding the red cock, at Thenseri hill with its golden walls touched by the moon.
615.nuance: மருள், delusion, is what the meaning cures, and the meaning is the one Murugan told உமை பங்காளர், Siva, the Siva-teaching story. தர்க்கங்கள் அற: the knowledge ends disputation. மன்றாடிக்கு அன்பு தரு may mean the one dear to the dancer in the hall, Siva, and is unsure.

source_issues: Song 615: one corrupt character in வயலு஡ரா (line 15), read as வயலூரா, 'lord of Vayalur'.
